title: Market scouting runway for model supply and fallback orchestration
creator: Sofia Patel
background: We need a repeatable way to assess short- and medium-term availability of open and licensed models across regions and vendors, quantify substitution costs (latency, accuracy, token-cost), and encode those signals into a canonical fallback orchestration policy used by routing and Dedicated capacity products. Current work is ad-hoc: procurement and ops scramble when a model becomes unavailable, degrading SLAs for high-value enterprise customers.
objective: Produce a defensible, operational 'supply runway' that maps model availability signals to automated fallback policies and procurement triggers so that routing, Dedicated, and Private deployments can maintain SLOs while minimizing cost and manual intervention.
success_criteria: A scoring rubric that predicts realistic substitution cost for 90% of models we serve within +/- 15% of observed production delta
Routing can automatically switch to a compatible fallback model with validated quality regression guardrails in <= 500ms decision window
Procurement playbook with alert thresholds that reduces manual procurement escalations by 70% in the next quarter
Dashboard surface with per-region availability and substitution-cost heatmap used by on-call and commercial teams
scope_in_scope: Inventories of models we currently serve (hosted + dedicated + private) and candidate substitutes
Scoring matrix that captures latency, cost-per-token, quantization compatibility, and observed quality delta against canonical eval sets
Integration points for routing policies (smart routing service) and Dedicated autoscaler triggers
A minimal procurement playbook with vendor contact templates and LL contract checklist
out_of_scope: Full rewrite of serving runtime — changes will be limited to policy layer and guardrails
Customer-specific bespoke model onboarding (this is a templated supply runway, not custom onboarding)

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Eval sets may not reflect customer-specific failure modes -> Mitigation: sample 5 high-value customers' prompt-sets after NDAs and build targeted eval cohorts

Risk: Vendor licensing prevents some substitutions in Private deployments -> Mitigation: flag licensing incompatibility in the rubric and exclude from automatic fallback; raise procurement alert instead
Risk: Quick switch causes cache/context mismatch and spikes latency -> Mitigation: add a lightweight warmup path that reuses KV cache heuristics and a conservative canary window
Risk: Over-automation leads to quality regressions -> Mitigation: require guardrail checks (LLM-eval thresholds) and human-in-the-loop approval for fallbacks with projected quality delta > 8%

decisions: Decision: Use a hybrid score = (0.4 * latency_rank) + (0.3 * quality_delta_rank) + (0.2 * cost_rank) + (0.1 * license_compatibility_rank). Rationale: latency-driven for product SLA risks while still considering cost and license constraints.
Decision: Automatic fallback allowed only when predicted quality delta <= 5% and cost increase <= 20%; otherwise trigger procurement workflow.
Decision: For Private deployments, automatic fallback is disabled by default; customers can opt into automatic fallback via an explicit config flag.
Decision: Add a short-lived 'warmup' fallback path that pre-populates KV cache to reduce first-token latency penalty when switching models
